problems.title: Convex angle averaging does not preserve the product-group law
problems.source_location: Appendix A.5.1, PDF pp.17–18; Proposition A.4 and proof, PDF pp.20–21
claim: The proposed map sends component rotations to \(\phi(R(\theta_1),\ldots,R(\theta_n))=R(\sum_iw_i\theta_i\bmod2\pi)\) and is asserted to be a homomorphism for fixed or learned convex weights.
analysis: Take \(G_1=G_2=\{I,-I\}\), weights \(w_1=w_2=1/2\), and \(g=h=(-I,I)\), using angles \(0,\pi\). Then \(gh=(I,I)\), so \(\phi(gh)=I\); but \(\phi(g)=\phi(h)=R(\pi/2)\), giving \(\phi(g)\phi(h)=-I\). A coordinatewise angular carry of \(2\pi\) becomes only \(\pi\) after half weighting. Without a fixed branch, even the representatives \(0\) and \(2\pi\) for the identity give different outputs. A branch makes a function but does not fix the exhibited group-law failure.
result: The claimed product-group homomorphism is false. This does not refute circular-mean equivariance under one common rotation or the empirical prediction results.
assumptions: The group domain includes the two-element rotation subgroup and positive half weights.
repair: Integer angle coefficients give well-defined torus homomorphisms. Alternatively, the paper’s circular mean \(s/|s|\), \(s=\sum_iw_iz_i\), is equivariant under a common rotation when weights are invariant and \(s\ne0\); it has a different guarantee. Keeping the unnormalized sum handles zero resultants globally.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a substantial invalid group-theoretic derivation of the sequence representation’s stated preservation guarantee, with an exact admissible group-law contradiction.

problems.title: The projected Stiefel operator is not an ambient rotation
problems.source_location: Section 2.3, PDF p.4; Section 2.5, PDF pp.5–6; Proposition A.3 and proof, PDF pp.19–20
claim: Proposition A.3 asserts \(VRV^\top\in SO(d)\) and identity action on the orthogonal complement when \(V^\top V=I_2\).
analysis: For \(d=3\), \(V=(e_1,e_2)\) and \(R=R(\pi/2)\), the operator sends \(e_3\) to zero and has determinant zero. Generally \((VRV^\top)^\top(VRV^\top)=VV^\top\), a rank-two projector rather than the ambient identity. However, Sections 2.3 and 2.5 already give the correct full lift, and an aligned base vector in the plane makes the embedding values coincide. The projected-circle conclusion survives.
result: The appendix’s ambient operator assertion is false, while its restricted-plane interpretation and earlier corrected construction survive. An implementation failure is not established.
assumptions: The ambient dimension exceeds \(2\); the base vector is unrestricted in the appendix statement.
repair: Use the existing full lift \(Q=I-VV^\top+VRV^\top\). Orthogonal plane/complement blocks give \(Q^\top Q=I\) and determinant \(1\). If projection is intended, restrict the rotation assertion to the plane.
problems.existing_correction_status: The correct complement-preserving formula already appears in Sections 2.3 and 2.5; reconciliation of the appendix is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The correct full-space lift and aligned-base special case already appear in the paper, limiting the demonstrated impact to an inconsistent supporting formulation.

problems.title: The reported regression pairs need a matched-evaluation definition
problems.source_location: Tables 15–16, PDF pp.31–32; Appendix A.9.2 and A.10, PDF pp.25–26
claim: The mRFP columns pair Pearson correlation and coefficient of determination for the same named variants. If they use one common nonconstant target/prediction vector and standard definitions, they must satisfy \(R^2\le r^2\).
analysis: Writing \(t=\sqrt{S_{pp}/S_{yy}}\) and \(d^2=N(\bar p-\bar y)^2/S_{yy}\), residual expansion gives \(R^2=r^2-(t-r)^2-d^2\le r^2\). The vanilla row has \(r=0.6875\) and \(R^2=0.8028\), while \(r^2=0.47265625\). The same conditional comparison fails in all thirteen printed mRFP rows, with the smallest gap over \(0.223\), beyond four-decimal rounding. However, separate checkpoints, subsets, target scales or fold/run aggregation can invalidate a direct shared-vector comparison; averaged correlations need not obey the squared-mean bound.
result: The table values are incompatible under a common-vector standard-metric interpretation. The paper does not supply enough evaluation records to establish that interpretation or identify a wrong column.
assumptions: Standard Pearson and test-set coefficient of determination on identical nonconstant paired vectors are required for the inequality.
repair: Identify sample IDs, prediction vectors, target scale, checkpoint, metric implementation and aggregation for both columns. Recompute matched metrics if that was intended; no replacement score is determined by correlation alone.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The exact compatibility identity is sound, but missing prediction-level and aggregation provenance prevents assigning a demonstrated empirical error.
